comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
2026-10-17, evidence for section 4 (a helper tells its maker) from two projects:

- A private project, 2026-10-13: its orchestrator watched up to ten worker panes with background `muster pane wait --pane ... --until blocked,stuck,idle` and rebuilt the pane list by hand about a dozen times. Closing a finished worker's pane ended the wait for all of them, since a wait fails when any pane it names closes. One worker sat idle for 35 minutes after an API connection error before anyone noticed. The orchestrator kept its workers' pane ids in a scratchpad file to find them again after compacting.
- muster's parallel-work round, 2026-10-16: the integrator hand-wrote a watcher polling `muster window --json`, and it misreported workers for an hour (tooling-feedback a_2j5RMfBLI).

Two gaps between section 4 and that evidence:

- **Idle.** Section 4 covers blocked and stuck. The 35-minute case was a helper whose turn ended on an API error and that posted nothing. Proposed: a helper that goes idle without having posted to its maker since it last went to work tells the maker too. A helper that reports and then goes idle stays silent.
- **Context.** Nothing to add: `compact_at` already compacts a helper once it is full enough.

`select(.maker == env.MUSTER_PANE)` replaces the pane-id files. Questions A and B are still waiting on amterp.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
amterp, 2026-10-07, on the hidden/headless note: "you could kind of imagine ... in the parallel work skill example, like the main integrator agent maybe like has some way to express with muster that these agents are sub agents or they belong to my group, and so therefore it has like the option to spawn them hidden, and there's some easy connected way to kind of see and like bring them forward, unhide them and see them." "This might take some design thought."

The idea that ties three notes together: a pane can belong to the agent that made it. Its sub-agents could then be made hidden (a_2die7jO4X) and quiet (a_2die7W9ru) by default, listed together under it, and brought forward together. A council or a parallel-work round is the motivating case: the human talks to the integrator, and the workers are the integrator's business.

Needs a MIP before building: what records the relation (the pane that ran `pane new`? a msg group?), what it changes by default, how it shows in the agent list and `muster window`, and what happens when the parent goes away. Build a_2die7jO4X and a_2die7W9ru first; this composes them.
title: 👪 An agent's sub-agents: made as its own, hidden and quiet, brought forward together
